title: Chemical Equilibrium
standard_text: Open and closed systems; reversible reactions and dynamic equilibrium; the equilibrium constant Kc and its expression; calculations with Kc (using a table of moles); Le Chatelier's principle and the effect of concentration, pressure and temperature; the effect of a catalyst; industrial applications such as the Haber process. (summary of the senior secondary Chemistry curriculum, SSS 3; WAEC and NECO syllabuses)
meta_desc: Free SSS 3 Chemistry worksheets (senior secondary curriculum, WAEC and NECO): dynamic equilibrium, le Chatelier's principle, equilibrium expressions, calculating Kc and equilibrium amounts and industrial processes. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: At equilibrium the forward and reverse rates are equal.
key_sub: Only temperature changes the value of Kc.
body_html:
How to think about it

In a closed system a reversible reaction reaches dynamic equilibrium: the forward and reverse reactions continue at the same rate, so the concentrations stay constant. For aA + bB ⇌ cC + dD, Kc = [C]ᶜ[D]ᵈ / [A]ᵃ[B]ᵇ; solids and pure liquids are left out. A large Kc means mostly products.

Le Chatelier's principle: when an equilibrium is disturbed, it shifts to oppose the change. Adding a reactant shifts it to the right; increasing pressure favours the side with fewer moles of gas; increasing temperature favours the endothermic reaction. A catalyst speeds up both reactions equally and does not shift the equilibrium.

Example

N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃ (exothermic). Temperature is raised. Effect on the yield of NH₃?

Endothermic direction is favoured.

Answer: it decreases

Example

Write Kc for H₂ + I₂ ⇌ 2HI.

Products over reactants

Answer: [HI]² / ([H₂][I₂])

Common mistakes

  • Thinking reactions stop at equilibrium.
  • Including solids in Kc.
  • Thinking a catalyst increases the yield.

faq.q: Why is the Haber process done at about 450 °C even though a lower temperature gives more ammonia?
faq.a: At low temperatures the rate is too slow; 450 °C is a compromise between rate and yield.

faq.q: What changes the value of K<sub>c</sub>?

items.q: An engineer wants more NO<sub>2</sub> from a brown gas mixture: N<sub>2</sub>O<sub>4</sub> ⇌ 2NO<sub>2</sub>, the energy change = +57 kJ. Which single change increases the amount of NO<sub>2</sub> at equilibrium?
c: The pressure is increased (the container is made smaller).
items.e: the energy change = +57 kJ, so the forward reaction is endothermic. Heating favors the endothermic direction.

items.q: What is a dynamic equilibrium?
c: the concentrations of reactants and products are equal
the forward and reverse reactions happen at the same rate, so concentrations stay constant
items.e: It needs a closed system.

items.q: What does a very large value of K (such as 10¹⁰) tell you?
c: at equilibrium there are mostly reactants
at equilibrium there are mostly products
items.e: K describes position, not rate.
